attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'won't' about GPT-4. 'By itself' is kept as a configuration qualifier. The proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: Reading the claim as broad competence on unfamiliar tasks, not infallibility, is ordinary and fair. Marcus gave no AGI definition or threshold, so the result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI's disclosure about its own model reports hallucinations and reasoning errors. This is relevant, but unreliability alone does not meet the support condition, which requires ruling out broadly general competence.

Researchers describe broad capabilities in an early GPT-4 version along with limitations. Their interpretation does not establish competence on arbitrary tasks, and it does not settle the claim either way.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has a company disclosure of limitations and a preprint claiming early, incomplete AGI. Neither independently establishes or rules out broad general competence for GPT-4 without external aids, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Unresolved.

semantics.note: 'I predict' with 'will need' is an unhedged forecast of necessity. In context, 'for that' refers to AI we can trust, which the proposition captures.

contract.note: Requiring evidence of necessity matches 'need'. 'Trustworthy', 'genuinely new' and 'at their very core' have no technical definitions, so any resolution would depend on how they are read, even though the contract flags this as false.

evidence.note: A February 2026 scientific synthesis reports continuing reliability limits. It says nothing about which architectures are necessary.

A September 2026 OpenAI disclosure about its own model reports alignment gains and remaining monitoring limits. It is not independent proof of trustworthy general AI and gives no architectural counterexample.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast that trustworthy AI will need explicit knowledge and world models at its core. No independently validated trustworthy general AI system appears in the packet, and there is no evidence about necessity. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all three 'won't' limits, the 'without external aids' qualifier and the Optimus/Rosie bar.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into three parts and treating separate controllers or planners as external aids are ordinary readings. Results would depend on how 'external aids', 'beat' and 'reliably' are read.

evidence.note: The ablation finds vanilla LLMs did poorly, but it does not isolate GPT-4 against Cicero. The Richelieu results that rival Cicero rely on added modules. This leans toward the Diplomacy limit but does not establish it.
Talk2Drive relies on an external Autoware controller, so it neither shows nor rules out reliable driving by GPT-4 alone.
Alter3 shows GPT-4 generating poses and motions. It does not test reliable, versatile household work.

reviews.rationale: This is a three-part forecast with no deadline. None of the items is a controlled evaluation of GPT-4 without aids on Diplomacy against Cicero, on driving, or on versatile robot guidance. Augmented systems do not count. Not one part is established or refuted, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The source says bad actors will eventually 'be able to' replicate and use knock-offs. The proposition drops 'be able to' and states that they actually will, which is stronger than what Marcus committed to.

contract.note: The support condition demands documented malicious deployment of a GPT-4-equivalent knock-off with safeguards removed. The words claim only that bad actors will gain the ability, so the contract is stricter than the statement. Linking the elements to one chain is otherwise reasonable.

evidence.note: Meta says its own downloadable Llama 3.1 405B is competitive with GPT-4. This shows availability, but parity is a company disclosure, and it shows no misuse or removed safeguards.

A news report says WormGPT variants built on Grok and Mixtral produced malicious output after researcher probing. There is no GPT-4 capability comparison, and the outputs are phishing and malware rather than narratives.
Forensic work probabilistically links an actual propaganda campaign to uncensored Llama-3-8B fine-tunes. It shows no capability comparable to GPT-4.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended 'eventually' forecast. The packet shows uncensored open models used in propaganda and GPT-4-class open weights. However, no item ties a GPT-4-equivalent knock-off to removed safeguards and malicious narratives, and parity rests only on Meta's own disclosure. Even under the weaker 'able to' reading this is unsettled. Unresolved.
